Pet-friendly stay at Paradox Singapore offers a glimpse into TA Global's hospitality ambitions
article:
[Note: The writer’s stay was hosted by the property as a complimentary media stay. EdgeProp Singapore maintains full editorial independence over its reviews.]

A staycation usually means packing a few basics into an overnight bag. For my recent stay at Paradox Singapore, the packing list was a little longer: leash, food, treats and other essentials for my pet Pomsky, Spencer, who was checking in with me.

The 476-room hotel along Merchant Road in the Clarke Quay precinct is among a relatively small number of hotels in central Singapore that welcomes pets. Its Pawcation Retreat package caters to dogs and cats weighing up to 15kg, across selected room categories.

Check-in was smooth, and the staff were friendly and welcoming towards both human and canine guests.

The Pawcation Retreat setup was already waiting in the room on our arrival, with pet supplies including a dog bed and bowl provided. Spencer also received two toys — a yellow plush and a dog-shaped fabric toy with a Peranakan-inspired print.

A separate basket was stocked with the likes of wet wipes and dental treats, along with other goodies as well as wet and dry food toppers.

Shortly after we entered the room, another set of welcome amenities were delivered: a bunch of fresh longans and a tiffin carrier filled with nibbles, including macarons, kueh and brownies.

More than a pet-friendly stay

While the Pawcation Retreat was the focus of my stay, Paradox Singapore positions itself as an urban resort catering to leisure, family and corporate travellers.

I stayed in a 30 sq m (323 sq ft) Premier Twin room, which came with two single beds. My window looked directly across to the CQ @ Clarke Quay lifestyle and entertainment hub, giving me a view of the riverfront.

The room was comfortable and well-equipped for a short stay, with complimentary WiFi, international power sockets and a writing desk with an ergonomic chair. The setup came in useful when I needed to get some work done during the stay. Other conveniences included a filtered-water tap and an in-room coffee and tea pantry.

Beyond the room, the hotel’s facilities cater to different types of guests. Families can make use of the swimming pool and children’s pool, while a whirlpool jacuzzi and poolside loungers offer options for those looking to relax. The gym operates around the clock, making it convenient for both leisure and business travellers to fit a workout into their schedules.

In terms of the hotel’s dining options, Ellenborough Market Café, its 250-seat riverside restaurant, serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, with a spread of Peranakan, local and international dishes. Other F&B offerings include Western à la carte dining at Blue Potato by the pool, drinks at Crossroads Bar, and alfresco dining overlooking the Singapore River.

Paradox Singapore also caters to weddings, conferences and corporate events. Its event facilities include 10 meeting rooms and the recently renovated, pillarless Merchant Court Ballroom, which features floor-to-ceiling windows and a 21m LED video wall. The ballroom can also accommodate wedding banquets for up to 420 guests.

Well-located in Clarke Quay

Location is another draw. The hotel sits beside the Singapore River, across from CQ @ Clarke Quay, with Clarke Quay MRT Station steps away. The dining and nightlife hubs of Clarke Quay and Boat Quay are also within walking distance.

With a dog in tow, I discovered another side to the precinct. Following its rejuvenation, CQ @ Clarke Quay has become increasingly pet-friendly, with pet hydration bays, waste bins and designated pet parking areas dotted around the development.

The riverside promenade provided an easy route for walks with Spencer, while Paradox Singapore allows pets at its alfresco dining area overlooking the river.

From hotel owner to hospitality brand

Paradox Singapore was formerly the Swissôtel Merchant Court. Malaysian developer TA Global acquired the hotel in 2009 for $250 million and rebranded it as Paradox Singapore in 2022.

The Singapore hotel forms part of TA Global’s wider hospitality portfolio, which spans properties in destinations including Vancouver, Whistler, Bangkok, Phuket, Kunshan and Sydney.

The creation of Paradox as TA Global’s own hospitality brand came in the aftermath of Covid-19, as the group moved towards operating its hotels under a shared identity.

Paradox Phuket was the first hotel to adopt the brand, rebranding in January 2022. Paradox Vancouver reopened in April that year following refurbishment and rebranding, becoming the flagship property of Paradox Hotels & Resorts.

Since then, TA Global has been progressively bringing hotels in its portfolio under the Paradox identity.

At Paradox Singapore, the ballroom was recently renovated, while its guest rooms are next in line for refurbishment.

The group is now bringing the brand closer to home with its upcoming Paradox KLCC in Kuala Lumpur — and extending its hospitality experience into residential living.

Bringing Paradox to KLCC

Paradox KLCC forms part of TA Global’s RM3 billion ($939 million) luxury integrated development on a freehold site in the prime Jalan P Ramlee nightlife strip, just 50m from the Petronas Twin Towers.

TA Global’s development comprises two towers. CloutHaus Residences is a 66-storey tower with 615 serviced residences, while the neighbouring 58-storey tower will house the 548-key Paradox KLCC hotel and the 242-unit Paradox Residences.

The connection between TA Global’s hospitality and residential businesses will go beyond sharing the same address.

CloutHaus residents will have access to services by Paradox such as a 24-hour concierge. Other conveniences such as housekeeping, laundry and dry-cleaning, grocery shopping and pet care are available à la carte.

CloutHaus was launched in Malaysia in late 2024 and was 40% sold as at July 2026, with buyers representing more than 20 nationalities. TA Global subsequently previewed the development to Singapore investors at Paradox Singapore over the weekend of July 25 and 26.

The serviced residences range from 549 to 1,216 sq ft, with one- to three-bedroom layouts. The project is scheduled for completion in 2029.

title: New ETFs Coming to SGX: S&P 500, NASDAQ-100 and MSCI World Explained
article:

That’s when DWS Group (XETRA: DWS) is scheduled to cross-list four
Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities
(UCITS) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) directly in Singapore and denominated in the Singapore dollar (SGD), making
investments in ETFs
tracking global heavyweight indexes more frictionless.
Before these listings, the London Stock Exchange (LSE) had been the go-to venue for local investors seeking tax-optimised global equity exposure.
With the new listings, local investors will be able to enjoy the same tax benefits with local operational advantages.
Meet the Four Xtrackers ETFs
The line-up spans US large caps, an equal-weight variant, tech-heavy NASDAQ stocks and global developed markets.
Crucially, all four are accumulating share classes, which
reinvest dividends
rather than paying then out.
That makes them less suitable for income investors.

Many Singapore investors hold US-domiciled ETFs like

The reason?
The lack of a US-Singapore tax treaty.

Thankfully, all four Xtrackers ETFs are sub-funds of an Irish entity.

Pick Your Strategy
Selecting between these listings depends on your asset allocation goals.
XUS vs EUS:
Both XUS and EUS draw from the same 500 companies in the S&P 500.
The difference lies in their weightings.
Market-cap-weighted XUS concentrates over 20% in tech giants like
NVIDIA
(NASDAQ: NVDA),
Apple
(NASDAQ: AAPL), and
Microsoft
(NASDAQ: MSFT), while equal-weighted EUS is periodically rebalanced to approximately equal weights.
XND for Tech Growth:
With about 60% in technology, and financial companies excluded by design, XND leans into tech growth but carries higher volatility.
XWR for Developed Equities:
Covering 23 developed markets with a 75% US weighting, the XWR ETF that tracks the MSCI World Index serves as a core global anchor, though it excludes emerging markets entirely.
Related articles:
Can You Build an AI Portfolio Entirely With ETFs?
The S$10,000 Bonus Challenge: Dividing Your Windfall Between SG REITs and US Growth
Operational Perks and Local Mechanics
Trading in SGD on SGX often avoids upfront currency conversion fees.
However, investors remain exposed to USD/SGD exchange rate fluctuations due to the the underlying foreign-currency assets (mainly USD).
Investors will have the flexibility of holding these ETFs in their individual Central Depository (CDP) accounts or managing them through a custodian broker.
Moreover, these four Xtrackers funds are expected to be eligible for the Supplementary Retirement Scheme (SRS), subject to your SRS operator and broker.
That lets investors put SRS savings, which already earn tax relief on contributions, to work in low-cost index funds.
However, they are not included under the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS), so CPF savings cannot be used.
Cash-strapped young investors can start with as little as one share and build up their holdings through
dollar-cost averaging
.
Get Smart: Building a World-Class Portfolio Locally
The new UCITS ETFs will bring global investing right to the doorstep of local investors.
The benefits are plentiful: ultra-low expense ratios, dividend tax savings, reduced US estate tax exposure, SRS eligibility, and Asian trading hours.
However, smart investors should choose ETFs that align with their financial goals, then adopt a long-term investing horizon and let structural fee and tax savings compound over time.

title: DBS and Jardine Matheson see more small trades after board lot size cut to 10 shares
article:
Shares for Singapore blue-chips DBS Group (DBS) (SGX:D05 ) and Jardine Matheson (SGX:J36 ) saw more small trades being executed after their board lot sizes were cut to 10 shares from 100 shares on Oct 5.

The reduction in lot sizes was one of the measures proposed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Equities Market Review Group after it concluded its work in November 2025. Under the Singapore Exchange’s (SGX) new rules, which took effect on Oct 5, securities priced above $10 and up to $100 had their lot sizes reduced to 10 shares, while securities priced higher than $100 had their lot sizes reduced to one share. Stocks priced below $10 will continue to be traded at a lot size of 100 shares.

The initial reduction applies only 11 stocks. Aside from DBS and Jardine Matheson, the other nine stocks include: Great Eastern (SGX:G07 ) , Haw Par Corporation (SGX:H02 ) , Jardine Matheson Southeast Asia (SGX:C07 ) , Keppel (SGX:BN4 ) , the Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) (SGX:O39 ) , Prudential (SGX:K6S ) , SGX (SGX:S68 ) , United Overseas Bank (SGX:U11 ) and Venture Corporation (SGX:V03 ) .

According to trading data from Bloomberg, more than 20,000 trades were executed in 10-share lots across all 11 stocks on Oct 5, higher than the more than 13,000 trades that were executed in 100-share lots. Around 55% of the trades for all 11 stocks were executed in trade sizes smaller than 100 shares.

With the exception of Prudential, which saw only two trades on Oct 5, the other 10 stocks were actively traded. 10-share lots were the most common trading size for nine of the 10 actively traded stocks, with DBS taking the lead at around 5,000 trades.

Jardine Matheson, on the other hand, recorded the strongest adoption of smaller trade sizes. Approximately 2,200 or one-third of its trades were executed in 10-share lots. Keppel was the only counter with an even split between 10-share lots and 100-share lots at around 1,000 trades each.

See also: SAS, SIAS and SGX announce new Youth Stock Ambassadors Programme

Last week, OCBC Securities announced that it was removing minimum commissions for online trades from Oct 5. Wilson He, managing director of OCBC Securities, says the move was meant to align with SGX’s reduction of board lot sizes.

“If we reduce the minimum board lot size, for example, on the banking shares, but we still charge high [minimum commissions], all the returns would basically be eroded by the commission fee. But if you charge proportionally, it is good for young investors who are starting with $500 and $1000, and it will become really meaningful,” He says.

title: Citi takes top spot in global IPO underwriting through September
article:
(Oct 6): Citigroup Inc took top spot for underwriters in global initial public offerings (IPOs) for the year through September after working on some of the biggest share sales in Asia and the US.

Citi was just ahead of Goldman Sachs Group Inc in the league tables, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Goldman was the top underwriter globally for equity offerings, a broader measure that also includes deals such as block trades and follow-on share sales, the data show.

Citi worked on transactions including National Stock Exchange of India Ltd’s US$2.4 billion listing in Mumbai in September, one of the biggest in the country’s history. It was lead global coordinator on SK Hynix Inc’s US$26.5 billion Nasdaq listing in July, the biggest-ever US share sale by a foreign company. It also had a role on SpaceX’s historic US$86 billion IPO in June.

The US lender has been adding dozens of senior investment bankers globally, including for its equity capital markets business. Last year, Citi hired Charlie Black from Goldman as head of North America technology ECM, and Bernal J Vargas III from JPMorgan Chase & Co as head of ECM in North America. It also named Rob Chan as head of ECM syndication in Asia.

title: World Bank lifts India GDP view, says Asia’s buffers too thin
article:
(Oct 6): The World Bank on Tuesday raised its growth forecast for India, saying strength in industry and services will help the economy weather a weaker monsoon and elevated energy prices.

The upgrade adds to a string of more optimistic assessments of the world’s fastest-growing major economy and comes a day before the Reserve Bank is expected to raise interest rates for the first time in nearly four years to contain rising inflation.

India’s economy will likely expand 7.1% in the fiscal year ending March 2027, half a percentage point more than the World Bank previously forecast. The projection, contained in its latest South Asia Development Update, is above the Reserve Bank of India’s 6.7% estimate, which is also widely expected to be upgraded on Wednesday.

“Domestic demand has been remarkably resilient,” Franziska Ohnsorge, the World Bank’s chief economist for South Asia, said in an interview. In India, that strength has been broad-based across private and government spending, investment and consumption, she said.

In its East Asia & Pacific Economic Update also released on Tuesday, the World Bank said economies in East Asia and the Pacific risk running out of firepower as they try to cushion the blow from an energy shock that’s set to persist into next year.

The region’s governments have responded more aggressively than peers elsewhere as the US-Iran war drove global prices up and they have relied more heavily on subsidies, the World Bank said.

See also: US, India officials signal trade deal talks at an impasse

The approach may be "unsustainable", it said, forecasting that Middle East oil exports won’t return to pre-conflict levels until mid-2027. “These measures may postpone the adjustments to behaviour required if the shock is persistent rather than temporary while also imposing fiscal costs and lowering foreign currency reserves.”

The World Bank cited Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam, which have all taken steps to suppress retail gasoline prices and have seen their dollar war chests depleted by between 15% and 40% this year.

For now, energy risks are outweighed by what the bank calls the “AI tailwinds".

See also: Wall Street’s US$10 bil India hospital bet sparks a fight over bills

It forecasts growth of 4.5% this year in East Asia and the Pacific, revising the figure up by 0.3 percentage points from the last forecast. That’s largely due to strong investment and exports led by the artificial-intelligence boom. The outlook for 4.4% growth next year was unchanged.

A longer-lasting energy shock could put more of that resilience at risk, especially if coupled with a downturn in the AI cycle and El Niño weather disruptions, the World Bank said. Higher energy costs have already weighed on manufacturing while the surge in transport prices has hit consumer demand.

“A renewed rise in energy prices may be more damaging to economic activity than initially observed, particularly as the drag from higher inflation and tighter financial conditions grows,” it said.

title: Greenpeace links 20 agricultural firms to Indonesian fires
article:
(Oct 6): Greenpeace has identified more than 20 palm, pulp and sugar companies, including several with links to Malaysia and Singapore, whose land concessions contained sources of smoke from fires that have ravaged Indonesia in recent months.

The environmental group worked with Indonesian NGO Pantau Gambut to detect 6,811 smoke-source points from Aug 1 through Oct 1 across Kalimantan, Papua, Sumatra, Sulawesi and Maluku, they said in a press briefing in Kuala Lumpur on Monday. These are locations that are likely sources of haze emitted by forest and peat fires, identified using satellite data.

Indonesia is battling one of its worst fire seasons in years as an intensifying El Niño raises temperatures and exacerbates drought, turning the landscape into a giant tinderbox. Also driving the uncontrolled blazes is the long-running use of slash-and-burn agricultural practices, which has proved hard to stamp out despite repeated attempts by Indonesian authorities.

The disaster has once again blanketed parts of Southeast Asia in toxic smog. Air quality was “very unhealthy” in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday, according to IQAir, and both the Malaysian capital and Singapore ranked among the top three most-polluted cities in the world.

At least four concessions with smoke-source points were found to have corporate links to Singaporean palm oil companies, the activists said, adding there was also a Malaysian plantation group on the list. The rest were Indonesian companies.

Greenpeace named firms including Singapore-listed First Resources Ltd and Malaysia-listed Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, both of which did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

See also: Why CEO succession is a strategy decision, not an HR replacement exercise

The findings indicate “a pattern of continued tolerance of fires to facilitate the clearing of land for new commercial development”, Greenpeace said in a statement.

Greenpeace called on Indonesia to halt the expansion of agricultural industries in environmentally vulnerable areas and revoke permits for concessions implicated in peatland destruction. The group also demanded stronger laws addressing transboundary haze, including clearer cross-border corporate accountability and measures designed to deter future fires.

Relief from the fires and smog is not expected until the end of October, when rains are forecast to start picking up, according to the latest seasonal outlook from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre. Indonesia’s national weather forecaster has said the rainy season will commence later than usual this year as a result of the powerful El Niño, keeping fire risks elevated for longer.

title: DeepSeek to raise at least US$12 bil in Tencent-backed funding
article:
(Oct 6): DeepSeek is close to securing at least 80 billion yuan (US$12 billion) in its latest round of funding, blowing past its own capital-raising target ahead of a landmark initial public offering in early 2027.

Battery pioneer Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd. and WeChat-operator Tencent Holdings Ltd have committed among the largest amounts in the current financing, which closes soon, people familiar with the matter said. DeepSeek initially sought about 50 billion yuan but interest outstripped expectations after the successful release of its latest AI model, the people said, asking not to be named as the details aren’t public. Based on term sheets signed, the final tally could approach 100 billion yuan, the people added.

DeepSeek’s funding sets the stage for one of the most highly anticipated Chinese market debuts in years. The company is riding high after the release of the V4 Flash, which reset expectations for cost versus performance against leaders Anthropic and OpenAI. That caps a strong run for founder Liang Wenfeng, whose startup has forged a reputation for technical breakthroughs since a 2025 model that matched the capabilities of Silicon Valley offerings at a fraction of the cost.

As with other AI players, DeepSeek requires huge amounts of capital to bankroll its ambitions in a potentially revolutionary technology. DeepSeek plans to deploy at least 160,000 of Huawei Technologies Co.’s top accelerators at a massive data center it’s building in Inner Mongolia, which may create one of the largest known clusters of Huawei AI chips. It’s publicly released software created with Huawei to program AI chips, a foray into a new arena in close partnership with the hardware leader. Rival Moonshot, meanwhile, is also targeting an early 2027 IPO after closing funding at a US$50 billion valuation.

Liang pledged in at least one meeting with investors this year he will keep developing open AI models while pursuing a broader goal of achieving artificial general intelligence. The hedge fund manager made it clear his main goal was to push the boundaries of the technology rather than monetization, Bloomberg News has reported.

While discussions around the current deal near an end, details may still change in final talks, the people said. DeepSeek had originally targeted a valuation of about 500 billion yuan in its financing. A CATL representative declined to comment, while Tencent had no immediate comment. DeepSeek didn’t respond to an emailed request for comment during a Chinese public holiday.

See also: Musk is a trillionaire again as SpaceX claws back post-IPO slump

DeepSeek has drawn enormous interest from would-be investors because it’s one of a clutch of companies that sit at the heart of China’s effort to compete globally on AI. Once the round closes, the next step should be to restructure the company to prepare for an IPO, the people said.

Tencent, which also landed the biggest investment in the startup at 10 billion yuan in a previous round of financing, aims to integrate AI into its platforms. CATL may be eyeing an increasingly lucrative business of supplying components to the industry, including for data centres.

The AI lab’s capital-raising had attracted its share of controversy. DeepSeek briefly suspended the deal after comments widely attributed to Liang about US-Chinese AI competition went viral on social media. Yicai reported in July that the billionaire entrepreneur talked about a reliance on Nvidia chips and China’s persistent lag in AI sophistication relative to the US.

See also: Google, Constellation near billion-dollar deal for nuclear power

Liang’s net worth more than doubled to around US$36 billion when DeepSeek closed its first round of external fundraising this summer. The AI startup grew as an offshoot from his hedge fund High-Flyer, which provided much of the initial support. Liang contributed again in the previous 50-billion-yuan round, which valued DeepSeek at roughly 350 billion yuan at the time.

title: Suzuki undercuts BYD as competition for cheap mini EVs heats up
article:
(Oct 6): Suzuki Motor Corp unveiled its first fully electric kei car, fuelling competition in Japan’s most important vehicle segment.

Including federal subsidies, the “e SKY” model will cost around ¥1.6 million when sales start in November, Suzuki said Tuesday. That’s cheaper than Nissan Motor Co’s top-selling Sakura EV and BYD Co’s first kei car the Chinese company introduced in July.

Kei cars are affordable, ultra-compact vehicles that account for more than a third of automobile sales in Japan. The arrival of the e SKY adds to signs that the country is becoming a key battleground for electric versions of the tiny cars, with Nissan, Honda, Daihatsu and now Suzuki offering them. Together, the Japanese brands control about 80% of the market.

Suzuki targets around 1,000 monthly sales for the tiny EV, which has a battery range of 310km and a base price of ¥2.1 million. Federal subsidies can bring its sticker down by around half a million yen. BYD said in July that its Racco kei car, which offers a minimum range of 210km will cost less than ¥2 million including subsidies.

In Japan, where EV uptake is far lower than in the US, Europe or China, Suzuki is betting that its first electric kei car can help lower the barrier for customers to make the switch from gasoline vehicles.

“We asked ourselves what kind of product would convince kei drivers to shift to an EV and this is our answer,” the model’s chief engineer Tomoyuki Tsubata told reporters in Tokyo. “We’re hoping this will help them recognise that option.”

title: MUFG commemorates Singapore-Japan 60th anniversary
article:
Japan’s largest banking group, MUFG Bank, (MUFG), commemorated 60 years of diplomatic relations between Singapore and Japan (SJ60) and its 70 years of presence in Singapore at a gala event with more than 300 dignitaries and guests on Sept 28.

The event was graced by Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore, Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade), and Chairman of the Monetary Authority of Singapore and His Excellency Hiroshi Ishikawa, Ambassador of Japan to Singapore, alongside senior leaders from government, business and finance, as well as MUFG senior executives from Japan and across the Asia Pacific (APAC).

Held at Capella Singapore, the evening reception brought together MUFG’s global, regional and Japanese corporate clients to celebrate one of Asia’s most enduring and successful bilateral partnerships.

Junichi Hanzawa, MUFG President and Group CEO, said in his toast remarks: “For MUFG, Asia is our second home market after Japan and an important growth region. Singapore plays a central role in our Asia strategy serving as our regional headquarters.

“MUFG is proud to grow alongside Singapore for seven decades, contributing to the enduring ties between Singapore and Japan, while creating value together with our customers, partners, and communities in Asia,“ he added.

President and CEO of MUFG Bank Masakazu Osawa, who previously served as the bank’s APAC chief executive based in Singapore, expressed gratitude for the deep trust and support that clients, partners, colleagues and other stakeholders have continued to provide MUFG: “What we have built is a unique platform, a client franchise that began with Japanese corporates and now extends across Singaporean and global companies, together with a broad network of partner banks, our strategic alliance with Morgan Stanley, and partnerships with leading digital businesses.

See also: Japan’s 10-year bond sale draws solid demand as yields top 3%

“Looking ahead to the next 60 to 70 years, we intend to make full use of these strengths. We will not only pursue solutions through even closer collaboration with our partners, but also connect clients with one another, creating new business opportunities, and continue to strengthen the flow of capital supporting Asia’s future,” he added.

MUFG opened its Singapore Branch in 1957, when the nation was laying the foundations of its modern economy. In 2013, MUFG established its regional headquarters here, reflecting its confidence in Singapore’s position as a financial hub and gateway to Asia.

MUFG’s strategic investments in APAC have exceeded US$20 billion, resulting in a powerful regional network comprising financial institutions in ASEAN and digital start-ups and expanding its physical footprint. Today, over 1,400 employees in Singapore provide regional support for clients and business activities across 18 markets in APAC.

See also: Daiwa says information on 110,000 clients may have been leaked

In his closing remarks, Yukinobu Saeki, MUFG Bank’s current Chief Executive for APAC said: “Time and again, Singapore has shown the world what ambition, resilience, and reinvention can achieve.

“As Asia Pacific continues to play a vital role in MUFG’s long-term growth and development, Singapore will remain at the heart of our Asia growth strategy,” he added.

title: Vietnam’s plan to expand LNG-fired power is well behind schedule
article:
(Oct 6): Vietnam’s push to use liquefied natural gas to meet surging electricity demand is well behind schedule, with only one of 18 gas-fired power projects expected to be finished on time.

Of the planned developments — which would have a combined capacity of more than 20GW — only LNG Hiep Phuoc is on schedule, Industry and Trade Minister Le Manh Hung said at a government meeting last week. Sixteen of the 18 projects have selected investors but just two have started construction, Deputy Industry and Trade Minister Truong Thanh Hoai said at the same meeting.

The delays threaten Vietnam’s plan for the super-chilled fuel to make up as much as 12% of its power mix by 2030. The country only started to import LNG in 2023 but is viewed by the global industry as a major potential growth market.

The problems are part of a wider issue with many generation and transmission projects falling behind schedule. The trade ministry warned last month the country faced the risk of power shortages from next year due to the delays. Vietnam’s goal of at least 10% annual economic growth through 2030 is adding pressure to the grid, with new factories, technology and infrastructure projects boosting power demand.

The LNG Hiep Phuoc project in Ho Chi Minh City is aiming to begin commercial operations by the fourth quarter of 2028, according to reports in local media. Of the other 17 planned gas-fired power stations, about five are supposed to be finished before the end of the decade.

See also: Singapore and World Bank launch ASEAN Power Grid Mobilisation Partnership

Most of the projects are struggling to complete land and site clearance, financing arrangements and power-purchase agreements, according to a government account of last week’s meeting. Acting Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc has ordered authorities to establish detailed timelines for each project to identify delays earlier.

The Southeast Asian nation remains dependent on coal for its electricity. The fossil fuel accounted for 46% of power generation last year, followed by hydro at 34% and solar at 8%, according to BloombergNEF. Vietnam’s LNG imports will reach 3 million tonnes by 2030, BNEF forecast, down from an estimate of 4.9 million tonnes made in 2025.

title: Ray Dalio warns China, Japan may pull back from US Treasuries
article:
(Oct 6): Billionaire Ray Dalio warned that the Treasury market is vulnerable to a pullback of demand from China and Japan, two of the US’s largest foreign creditors, highlighting a potential pain point for a sector that has endured wild swings this year.

The US relies on foreign capital for about a third of its debt, and a lot of that is coming from Japan and China, Dalio, the founder of Bridgewater Associates, said on Bloomberg Television in Singapore on Tuesday.

“The Chinese don’t want to continue to accumulate — there are geopolitical issues as well as economic issues,” he said. “When you have a debtor-creditor relationship and you have an adversary relationship, that’s a very difficult dynamic.”

He added that Japan has lent “a lot of money” that the country now wants to take back.

His comments came after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tried to reassure investors that a mix of economic growth and spending restraints will “very quickly” start to alter the path of US government borrowing. Bessent, speaking at a fireside chat in Pennsylvania on Monday night, said the government would start “bending the curve”.

Dalio’s remarks suggest the Treasury secretary has a long way to go to convince some investors. The Bridgewater founder repeated his warning that the US faces a potential debt crisis within three years, arguing that some borrowers are already starting to feel the squeeze.

See also: UK job slump longer than during financial crisis, PMI says

Bonds have extended their months-long slide this week. Yields on 10-year US Treasuries are trading at around 5.3%, hovering at levels last seen in 2002. Global bonds have lost 3% this year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Treasuries have fallen 2.8% in the same period.

The US Treasury market has been vulnerable this year to increasing investor jitters over government borrowing and inflation risks. Similar concerns have roiled sovereign debt markets elsewhere, with France in particular becoming a trouble spot after its 10-year bonds suffered their worst quarter since the birth of the euro.

See also: AMRO raises Asean+3 2027 growth forecast to 4.1% but expects higher inflation

Dalio said France had “reached its borrowing limit”, adding to investor concerns that the country’s under-fire debt market was facing a moment of reckoning.

Japan — the biggest foreign owner of US Treasuries — and China have already been paring their holdings.

Japan saw a US$12.8 billion ($16.4 billion) drop in its Treasury holdings in July to US$1.1 trillion. That month included action by Japanese authorities to prop up the yen. Recent figures from the country’s Finance Ministry indicated that Tokyo likely sold a portion of its holdings of foreign securities to help fund its yen intervention moves.

Mainland China has seen its official Treasuries pile drop from a peak of US$1.3 trillion in 2013 to around US$618 billion in July, the third-largest foreign holding. However, market analysts suggest that figure may be an undercount as holdings of other countries such as Belgium likely include Chinese custodial accounts. The latest figures for Belgian Treasury holdings stood at US$470.7 billion.

Dalio also spoke of increasing funding strains for large technology companies that are investing in artificial intelligence. That means so-called hyperscalers are starting to encounter issues.

“Before, they would raise equity and now they need to come to debt,” he said, warning that several factors could cause the AI bubble to burst. “Something like a wealth tax would have that effect, or having to pay back loans.”

title: Thai inflation accelerates again with floods adding price risk
article:
(Oct 6): Thailand’s inflation accelerated for a second straight month in September, moving closer to the central bank’s upper limit as severe flooding adds to the risk of higher food prices.

The consumer price index rose 2.82% in September from a year earlier, accelerating from 2.53% in August, Commerce Ministry data showed Tuesday. Still, the reading was below the 3.1% median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists.

Despite the pickup, inflation remains within the Bank of Thailand’s 1%-3% target range but brings it closer to the upper bound after a prolonged period of subdued price pressures.

Higher oil and processed-food prices drove much of the acceleration, reflecting elevated raw-material costs and the conflict in the Middle East, according to Nantapong Chiralerspong, director-general of the Commerce Ministry’s Trade Policy and Strategy Office. Prices of eggs, chicken, vegetables and fruit also increased as changing weather conditions affected supplies.

Food and energy together make up the largest share of Thailand’s consumer-price basket, making households particularly sensitive to swings in oil prices and disruptions to agricultural supplies.

See also: Bangkok floods hit Thai Airways, Honda as disruption spreads

Those pressures are unlikely to fade quickly. The ministry expects inflation to continue accelerating in the fourth quarter as elevated oil prices feed into transportation and processed-food costs. Recent flooding is expected to add about 0.1 percentage points to inflation by disrupting fresh-food supplies.

The ministry now expects full-year inflation of 1.8%-2.2%, compared with its previous range of 1.5%-2.5%.

Thailand is facing similar price pressures to other energy-importing economies in the region. Inflation in the Philippines accelerated for the first time in five months in September and remained above its central bank’s 3% target after the Middle East conflict drove up global oil prices.

See also: Singapore’s annual growth rate to stabilise at 2.7% for the next decade, amid wider divergence in Southeast Asia

For Thailand, floods are emerging as an additional risk. Severe inundation in Bangkok and dozens of provinces has disrupted transportation and businesses while further heavy rain could damage crops and complicate food distribution, putting upward pressure on prices.

The acceleration is unlikely to materially change the Bank of Thailand’s policy stance for now. Officials have signalled they are prepared to look through temporary price spikes while maintaining support for an economy expected to grow only about 2%-2.5% this year.

The central bank kept its benchmark rate at 1% for a third consecutive meeting in August. Its next decision is scheduled for Oct 28.

On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.25% in September, compared with 0.56% in August. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 1.5% from a year earlier, up from 1.44%.

title: Moonshot said to eye early 2027 IPO after value hits US$50 bil — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 6): Moonshot AI has closed the final round of private fundraising at a valuation of about US$50 billion ($64 billion) and is heading towards an initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong in the first quarter of next year, according to people familiar with the matter.

The Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) champion has also begun laying the groundwork to start gauging investor sentiment through early-look meetings starting as early as this month, some of the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

Moonshot is one of the biggest stars of China’s AI scene, bursting onto the global stage in July with the debut of Kimi K3, an open model that goes nearly toe-to-toe with leading platforms from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic on some metrics. Its planned IPO is one of the most hotly anticipated deals in Hong Kong, where fundraising driven by the industry is setting fresh records. The company is considering raising up to US$5 billion in the deal, people familiar with the matter have said.

It is unclear how the valuation or the IPO timeline may be affected by tighter oversight of China’s AI industry after regulators opened a data-security probe into DeepSeek and Moonshot, according to The Information, adding to broader concerns over governance and safety.

Deliberations are ongoing and the timing of the IPO might still change, the people said. Moonshot representatives didn’t respond to requests for comment during a Chinese public holiday.

The company’s valuation has risen steadily through a series of fundraising efforts. A previous round this summer valued it at US$31.5 billion. Moonshot’s annual recurring revenue, a gauge of future sales, is expected to rise to US$2 billion by December from the current US$1 billion, people familiar with the matter have said. The company achieved US$300 million of ARR in June, Bloomberg News reported earlier.

The Beijing-based AI lab previously added Bank of America Corp as overall coordinator for the transaction alongside sponsor banks China International Capital Corp, Deutsche Bank AG and Goldman Sachs Group Inc, people familiar with the matter said previously. The company has filed confidentially for the IPO, they said.

Founded in early 2023 by Yang Zhilin, a former Tsinghua University professor who previously worked at Meta Platforms Inc and Alphabet Inc’s Google, Moonshot counts Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, Tencent Holdings Ltd and 5Y Capital as its backers.

title: Japan’s 10-year bond sale draws solid demand as yields top 3%
article:
(Oct 6): Japan’s 10-year government bond auction Tuesday saw stronger demand than the 12-month average as elevated yields underpinned buying.

The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.76 compared with 3.29 at the previous sale and a 12-month average of 3.21. Bond futures pared their losses after the result.

The benchmark 10-year yield hit 3.115% on Tuesday, matching its highest level since 1996. A sale of the same tenor last month passed smoothly after yields reached 3%.

Yields above 3% helped draw solid demand at the auction, said Takuya Onizawa, fixed income strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities. Concerns over fiscal expansion and the risk that the Bank of Japan is falling behind the curve on inflation have not disappeared but the appeal of the higher yield outweighed those worries, he said.

In another sign of strong demand at the auction, the tail or gap between average and lowest-accepted prices was 0.02, compared with 0.12 last month.

See also: Daiwa says information on 110,000 clients may have been leaked

The domestic backdrop has become somewhat more supportive of bonds. Expectations for October rate hikes in both Japan and the US have receded while Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s administration has sought to dispel concerns that it favours reflationary policies or would pressure the BOJ to keep borrowing costs low.

Still, heightened global risks are adding to uncertainty. Treasuries saw renewed selling pressure, pushing longer-dated yields to fresh multi-decade peaks and extending a months-long slide. Meanwhile, mounting fiscal concerns in France have fuelled a selloff in government debt, adding to volatility across global bond markets and making investors more cautious about taking duration risk.

Attention now turns to Thursday’s 30-year bond auction which will provide another test of investor demand for longer maturities.

See also: Northern Japanese banks mull merger with US$82 bil in assets

The rise in Japanese yields has broader consequences at home. Higher government borrowing costs increase the expense of servicing Japan’s large debt burden and can feed through to corporate and household financing costs, potentially weighing on investment.

title: Musk is a trillionaire again as SpaceX claws back post-IPO slump
article:
The fortune of the world’s richest person jumped by US$65 billion ($83 billion) on Monday to US$1.04 trillion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, as the value of his stakes in SpaceX and Tesla Inc rose. SpaceX shares are up 13% since the start of October while Tesla has gained 6.7%.

It marks the first time in three months that the 55-year-old tech mogul’s fortune has required 13 numerals. He became the world’s first trillionaire in June when SpaceX surged in the wake of its record-breaking initial public offering, but quickly lost that crown as shares then slumped on concerns about the company’s sky-high valuation.

As of late July, Musk’s US$600 billion-plus wealth decline from its peak exceeded the net worth of anyone who had ever been on Bloomberg’s list of the world’s 500 richest people, other than Musk himself.

The latest gains have been fuelled by renewed optimism at both companies. On Monday, analysts at Morgan Stanley called SpaceX one of the cheapest ways to play “the strong optionality” of the space and intelligence sector, adding to a rally in which shares of the space, artificial intelligence and social media company have rebounded 58% from an August low.

And last week, Tesla reported better-than-expected sales for the third quarter.

See also: Google, Constellation near billion-dollar deal for nuclear power

Musk’s stake in SpaceX and Tesla makes up more than 98% of his net worth, according to Bloomberg’s wealth index.
